name: Texas Coastal Management Program grants
summary: Reimbursement grants for coastal projects on public land in the Texas coastal zone, including habitat creation and restoration, from federal NOAA and GOMESA funds. Eligible applicants include 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) nonprofits with a Texas office.

amount.note: Up to $5 million for GOMESA-funded projects

steps: Supporting documents, work plan and budget, if conditionally selected

eligibility.rule: Nonprofit applicant is registered as a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) and has an office in Texas
Project is located within the Coastal Zone Boundary
Project occurs on publicly owned land, or qualifying non-federal lease or easement land
Project is consistent with CMP goals and enforceable policies
Project does not cause adverse effects to coastal natural resource areas
Project directly addresses or implements a listed funding priority
GOMESA project meets a GOMESA authorized use

documents: Available permits (GOMESA; if applicable for NOAA)
Draft site plan and site photos (GOMESA), or site plan, photos or final designs (NOAA §306A)

calls.label: Cycle 32
calls.note: Match of 40% applies to NOAA-funded projects; GOMESA-funded projects need none.

applicant_types.quote: Councils of governments and other regional governmental entities within the coastal zone boundary • The Galveston Bay Estuary Program • The Coastal Bend Bays and Estuaries Program • Nonprofit Organizations*

geography.quote: Projects must be located within the Coastal Zone Boundary established by the Texas Legislature in 1995.

access.quote: Applications must be submitted through the GLO's Coastal Resources Application Portal (https://txglo.smapply.us/).

amount.quote: Applicants may request up to a maximum of $5 million in GOMESA funding.

co_finance_required.quote: Applicants requesting NOAA funds must provide a local and/or third-party match of 40% of the total project cost to comply with federal matching requirements.

effort.quote: CMP Review Team reviews applications and conducts site visits, if necessary.

submit additional supporting documentation, a draft work plan, and a budget narrative, which will be used by CMP staff to further determine funding status. If the applicant and the GLO mutually agree on project scope and budget, and all supporting documentation is received by November 11, 2026

eligibility.quote: Nonprofit organizations applying for funding must be registered as a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) and have an office located in Texas.
Projects must be located within the Coastal Zone Boundary established by the Texas Legislature in 1995.

Projects must occur on publicly owned land (local government-owned or state-owned land) and cannot occur on private or federally owned land or land owned by a nonprofit organization unless there is a perpetual lease or conservation easement in place.
Proposed projects must be consistent with the CMP goals and enforceable policies to be eligible for funding.
Applicants must demonstrate that the proposed projects will not cause adverse effects to coastal natural resource areas (see Appendix I).
Projects must directly address and/or implement a funding priority listed below.
CMP GOMESA projects must meet a GOMESA authorized use (see Appendix E).

co_finance.quote: Applicants requesting NOAA funds must provide a local and/or third-party match of 40% of the total project cost to comply with federal matching requirements.

after_award.quote: Subrecipients will submit progress reports, deliverables, and reimbursement requests to the GLO via the CMPReceipts@glo.texas.gov either monthly or quarterly. Reporting frequency is determined by project and entity type.
NPS related projects will need to quantify the amount of pollution the project successfully reduces in the final report.

documents.quote: Include project budget • Location Map • Available Permits • 1-3 Letters of Support
